title: The Three Plagues against the Enemy: how self-love is contained, refined, and finally sealed
arc: The teaching narrates the three discrete operations by which Divine Truth defeats the proprium across the three cosmic ages: an initial binding when the Light first descends and contains self-love, a middle refining in which the Great Fire separates and gathers inward what is hidden in matter, and a final fixing in which the unredeemed residue is split apart forever — male into the bolos, female into the tomb.
reading:
This chapter speaks of the Enemy — the Darkness, the King of Darkness as the proprium personified — and of the three bitter plagues, three wars, and three dangers that the Light has inflicted upon him. The threefold structure is not rhetorical: it is the fullness of process, the complete cycle by which self-love is dealt with across the three cosmic ages. Each plague is a discrete operation of Divine Truth at a distinct level of the spiritual drama, and together they exhaust the work of redemption from the side of what must be subdued.

The first plague is the cosmogonic war. Here the teaching describes how those who had gone forth from the King of Darkness were separated back to his own Land of Darkness, while he himself was taken from the midst and "bound in the Living Principle." Read correspondentially, this is the descent of the First Man: Divine Truth lowering itself into the realm of self-love so that the proprium, in the very act of seizing the Light, is itself caught and contained. The proprium believes it is reigning — and in a sense in this first war it does reign over the descended Light — but the binding is mutual, and what is decisive is that self-love is now held fast within the Living Principle, the very life it tried to devour. This is the first containment: the cosmic capture of evil through accommodation.

The second plague is the present cosmic age, the time of refining. The teaching marks it as "the time when there is a release-forth, a separation-forth, a dividing in the Great Fire." This Great Fire is divine love operating as judgment within the natural — the purifying ardor under which mingled states are sorted. Within it the icons, "all those things that are hidden" in the natural mind, are shaken forth, dissolved as concealments, and then gathered inward according to the first type — that is, restored to the original pattern in which they existed before the mingling. This is the regenerative middle: the Lord's continual work of pulling refined truth out of darkness and conjoining it back to its first form, while the corrupt residue is rebound into its own bondage. It is the discriminative work of the cosmos viewed from its negative side: every act of gathering inward is at the same time a plague upon the Enemy, because each truth recovered is a piece of his hoard taken from him.

The third plague is the consummation. Here the carrying-off in the last era separates every thing finally and forever — male from female. In the spiritual reading these are not sexes but the two poles of evil: the active falsity-from-self-love (the masculine, generating principle of the Enemy) and the corrupt receptive matrix that bears its forms (the feminine, the Enthumesis of Death, Hyle). The male is bound into the bolos, the final compacted clod where unredeemed self-love is sealed eternally; the female is gathered inward to the tomb, the state of permanent spiritual death. Stone — confirmed and immutable — is set in their midst, fixing the boundary forever. This is the eschatological seal: not annihilation but eternal binding, the proprium held in its own chosen state without further power to mingle.

The closing image gathers the whole. The "fruit of the Enemy" — what self-love has borne as its produce — comes to be in a heaven of its own, but a heaven that is "bitter and hard, in which there is no dissolution forth." It is the perfect inversion of the true heaven: where the Land of Light is conjunction, sweetness, and living interchange, this fixed state of evil is permanent disjunction, bitterness, and frozen separation. The Enemy himself is "split with splittings forever, separated forth forever" — the very work he did against the Living Soul (scattering, mingling, dividing) returned upon him as his own eternal condition.

So the teaching shows the complete logic of how the proprium is overcome. It is first contained by descent, then continually unmade by the refining fire of regeneration, and finally fixed in its own residue. What looks from one side like three plagues against the Enemy is, from the side of the Light, the three movements of a single redemption: capture, separation, and consummation. The reader is being shown that the work already accomplished in the first war and the work now proceeding in the Great Fire both move toward the same end — a state in which all that can be gathered inward is gathered, and all that cannot is sealed apart, so that mingling itself ceases and the Living Principle stands free.
